content.caseIdentity: In re Delhi Laws Act, 1912, AIR 1951 SC 332
content.facts: The Court examined statutory provisions delegating legislative power to the executive.
questionsBeforeCourt: What legislative functions may constitutionally be delegated?
What essential legislative functions cannot be delegated?
What is the constitutional source and permissible scope of delegated legislative power?
content.ratioDecidendi: The legislature may delegate ancillary functions but cannot abdicate its essential legislative policy-making function.
content.holding: The Court laid down the foundational excessive-delegation principle.
content.relevance: Use as the leading Indian authority on permissible delegation.
